finding.claim: GET /rss passes the unvalidated query parameter u straight to open-uri's URI.open, which fetches any http(s)/ftp URL the server can reach, follows redirects, and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the client. This is in-band SSRF to arbitrary internal hosts, including cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254.
finding.source: app.rb:8 params[:u] (Sinatra query-string parameter, attacker-controlled, unauthenticated)

trace.note: get "/rss" route; no auth or other guard on the route
params[:u] flows directly into URI.open; no scheme, host, IP, or port check
open-uri matches the scheme regex, calls URI.parse, then performs the network request, following http<->https redirects by default
response body truncated to data[0, 400] and returned to the caller, so the response is visible to the attacker (in-band, not blind)

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. No allowlist of hosts (contrast with TRUSTED at app.rb:5, which is only used on /trusted). No scheme restriction (ftp:// is accepted as well). No resolved-IP check, so private, loopback, and link-local addresses are reachable, and DNS rebinding would also apply. No redirect control. No port restriction. Adjacent but separate issue: when the string has no scheme, open-uri falls back to File.open, which is a local file read (path traversal class, not SSRF); I did not verify the file:// behaviour under this Ruby version.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /rss route (app.rb:7-10) has no auth, host allowlist, scheme check, or IP check before URI.open at app.rb:8. TRUSTED (app.rb:5) is referenced only by the /trusted route at app.rb:14, which is a separate handler and does not guard /rss.
verdict.reason: params[:u] at app.rb:8 is an unauthenticated query parameter passed straight to URI.open with no closing guard, and the response is returned in-band, truncated to 400 bytes, at app.rb:9.
